newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel 1996 inflation seen at 9-11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israel 1996 inflation seen at 9-11.5 pct.

text.p: Economists have given estimates that Israel's 1996 inflation rate will be nine percent to 11.5 percent against the government's target of 8-10 percent and 8.1 percent inflation in 1995.
Bank Hapoalim forecast 1996 inflation of 9.0 percent while economists from the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce predicted inflation will be 11.5 percent.
Since the beginning of the year the consumer price index (CPI) has increased 7.3 percent, or 12.9 percent in annual terms.
Hapoalim estimated the CPI in August grew 0.6 percent, following a rise of 0.3 percent in July, while the federation predicted August's CPI increased 0.4 to 0.5 percent.

August's CPI, which will be announced on September 13, was affected by a 13.3 percent hike in public transportation fares while clothing and shoe prices fell an estimated two to three percent. Housing, fruit and vegetable prices remained stable last month.
Bank Hapoalim said preliminary data indicate M1 money supply grew only 0.9 percent in August after surging 4.5 percent in July.
